catalog.summary: Group of controls with arrow-key navigation.

wiring.aria-label: the consumer's own, and the toolbar writes none of its own
wiring.aria-orientation: written on the root only when vertical, and on a separator always, perpendicular to the bar
wiring.aria-disabled: an item that says it stays in the ring; a native disabled attribute is skipped
wiring.aria-label on the overflow trigger: the count of what is hidden, from `label`; a string the consumer states is used verbatim
wiring.disabled on the overflow trigger: the platform's own `:disabled`, from a `<fieldset disabled>` around the bar. The family writes no `data-disabled` and declares no `disabled` state, because it does not own the capability.

keyOwners.inferred: a text entry, a select, a slider, a spin button or a contenteditable keeps the keys of the flow axis

keyboard.effect: moves focus into the bar, which holds one tab stop however many controls it has
keyboard.focus: the control that last had focus, or the first that is not disabled

keyboard.effect: moves to the next control in a horizontal bar, wrapping at the end and from row to row when the bar wrapped
moves to the previous control in a horizontal bar, wrapping at the start
moves to the next control, duplicating ArrowRight in a horizontal bar as the pattern permits
moves to the previous control, duplicating ArrowLeft in a horizontal bar as the pattern permits

keyboard.focus: the first control that is not natively disabled
the last control that is not natively disabled

checkedValues.reason: Fluent's toolbar holds the checked state of the controls inside it. `button` already ships `pressed`, and an exclusive set of segments is toggle-group in wave 8; a family holding another family's state is the desync docs/state-and-events.md exists to prevent.

arrangement.reason: gap, alignment, stacking and a joined bar belong to button-group, which is what a run of joined actions inside a toolbar is. The bar's own gap comes from its size step, and the spacer part is what pushes a run to the end.

itemWrappers.reason: Radix and Base UI wrap each item in a component of their own. Items are found by being focusable instead, so this library's own button, link, checkbox and text-field drop in unwrapped; an element that cannot hold focus is not an item, which is stated in the anatomy.

pagingControls.reason: a scrolling toolbar reveals its controls with the arrow keys, which reach every item; no surveyed toolbar draws paging buttons, and the menu is the answer the field agrees on, which `overflow="menu"` now is.

disabled.reason: Base UI alone ships a disabled toolbar. A container cannot disable controls it does not own, and a bar that refuses interaction while its controls still look operable is the defect packages/styles/src/states.test.mjs exists to prevent. The platform already answers it in two lines: <fieldset disabled> around the bar disables every control inside it natively, which also takes them out of the ring, because a natively disabled control cannot be focused.

overflowPriority.reason: Fluent ranks items with `priority` on `OverflowItem`. A priority is a way of saying "hide this one", and the bar is not supposed to have an opinion about which control matters — the author already stated that by placing it. What must stay visible has nowhere to go, which is one fact in one place instead of two knobs over one question.

overflowSection.reason: Kendo's section mode moves the tools' own components into the popup. A `menu` surface holds `menuitem`s and the controls in a bar are the consumer's own buttons and fields, so the counterpart is authored here instead: anything `menu`'s item types express is already reachable, and a run of live controls in a layer is a `popover` with a `toolbar` inside it.

collapsedState.reason: the set that does not fit is read from the browser. A controlled pair over it would let a consumer assert that a bar fits when the layout says it does not, and the DOM would then contradict the model — the reason `measurement` is not mutable either. The fact is reported instead: the count in the DOM and one callback per change.

counterpartDerivation.reason: Primer rebuilds each hidden control as an `ActionList.Item` from a `ChildProps` object, which it can do because the item types are its own four. The items here are anything focusable, so what a control becomes in the surface is written beside it — `overflow` on the `item` or the `group` — and a unit that writes nothing cannot be hidden.

roleGuidance.reason: the APG uses the role for three or more controls. A role that disappears when a permission filter removes a button is a semantic changing behind the author, so the guidance is documented and the consumer decides.

collapse.order: the bar's own order, reversed: the last unit that can give way is the first that does
collapse.pinned: a unit that declares no counterpart, which is every unit that is not an `item` or a `group` carrying one
collapse.trigger: hidden until the first unit gives way, and measured in the same synchronous pass that reveals it
collapse.separator: hidden when no visible unit follows it, and rendered as a menu separator when it sits between two collapsed units
collapse.degradation: a bar whose pinned units alone exceed it scrolls rather than clipping, which is also what `menu` with no `overflow` part does
collapse.focus: moved to the trigger before the unit holding it is hidden, because a hidden control drops focus on `body`
collapse.measurement: @slotted/core/overflow — `collapseState` for the arithmetic, `createCollapse` for the DOM
collapse.container: the room is the bar's own width, observed on the bar, so the layout around a bar with overflow=menu gives it a width that does not derive from its own content: a bar sized by its content is the trigger alone once everything has folded, it does not grow when its container does, and what folded never returns. A flex item holding it takes a zero basis and grows; a bar that stands at the end of its row fills the room and aligns its controls to the end
collapse.reports: `data-collapsed` on the root carries the count, and the root emits it once per change
